input: Draft talking points for my next performance review

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Performance reviews can cover accomplishments, growth areas, compensation, promotion, or all of the above — knowing the focus changes which points to prioritize.
Whether this review is with a direct manager, skip-level, or a panel affects tone, depth, and how to frame points.
The user's role, industry, and seniority level heavily influence the language, metrics, and examples that will land well.
Knowing the timeframe (e.g., review is tomorrow vs. in two weeks) shapes how detailed and polished the output needs to be.
Some people want to lead with data and metrics; others prefer narrative storytelling — this affects how each point is structured.
The user may want to walk away with a raise, a promotion, a development plan, or simply positive feedback — the goal shapes every point.
Whether they need a written document, a bullet list, or a script for speaking aloud determines the format and length of the output.

gold.taskTitle: Draft talking points for performance review
gold.taskDescription: Prepare a set of talking points the user can use in their upcoming performance review conversation.

questions.title: What is your main goal for this review?
questions.description: Is the user aiming for a promotion, a raise, a strong rating, a development plan, or simply a positive conversation? This determines the entire strategic angle of the talking points.

questions.title: Which topics should the talking points cover?
questions.description: Should the points focus on recent accomplishments, areas of growth, future goals, or a mix? Knowing what to include vs. leave out defines the scope.

questions.title: What is your role and industry?
questions.description: The user's job title, function, and industry determine the right vocabulary, metrics, and examples that will resonate in context.

questions.title: Who will you be speaking with in the review?
questions.description: Is this with a direct manager, a skip-level leader, an HR panel, or someone else? The audience affects how formal and how detailed each point should be.

questions.title: How soon is the review taking place?
questions.description: The timeline determines how much refinement and preparation is realistic before the session.

questions.title: Do you prefer data-driven points or narrative-style ones?
questions.description: Some people lead with numbers and measurable impact; others prefer story-based examples. This shapes how each talking point is framed.

questions.title: What format do you need the output in?
questions.description: Should the result be a concise bullet list, a structured written document, or a spoken script? This determines the length and presentation of the final deliverable.
